about: What each check on every PR catches, in my words. tests: id from node tools/run-tests.mjs --list; ci: job key from .github/workflows/ci.yml; budget: the checked-in file whose numbers it enforces (the build fails if the file is missing). A check without an entry still shows, marked 'description to come'. label replaces the raw check name where that name has wording the public page leaves out. coming: gates in flight; a PR number shows its live status.

types.catches: A type error anywhere in the project (tsc --noEmit).

lint.catches: Shared code that isn't deterministic, per-tick allocation in hot files, unowned GPU resources, raw URL flags, type-only imports written as values.

formal.catches: A TLA+ model, or the code regions it names, changing since the model last passed its checker. It compares hashes of the code; it does not re-run the checker.
formal.label: TLA+ models still match the code they describe

flags.catches: Feature-flag defaults, URL and stored overrides, and the query string the registry builds, not behaving as documented.

bundles.label: Playtest report uploads (hostile input, size caps)
bundles.catches: The playtest report endpoint: unknown fields are dropped, oversized or malformed bundles, hostile diagnostics and broken uploads are refused, and the folder's count and size caps hold.

auto.catches: Automatic summary rows: hostile rows are refused, unknown fields dropped, and the endpoint's own limits and folder cap hold over HTTP.

triage.catches: Playtest bundles not grouped into the expected clusters by fingerprint, or a callsign or message reaching a public output.

ab.catches: Bundles not split by transport arm with the right medians and per-minute rates, a link counted twice, or a callsign or message reaching the output.

gate.catches: The shared flag parser for verifiers accepting an unknown flag, a missing or non-numeric value or a stray argument, or a verifier passing when it found nothing to check.

size.catches: Gzip bytes of entry, boot, worker and lazy JavaScript going over the budget, or more than 5% under it until the budget is lowered.

farbake.catches: A far-away stand-in file whose header or index entry doesn't match (fails). One that is stale or not baked yet is only reported for now.

assets.catches: A new art, sound or font file with no recorded source and licence.

dmath.catches: A math function that gives different bits than the recorded vectors, which would split client and server.

movement.catches: Ledge climbs (up to 2.1 m climbed, 2.2 m not), slides, air steering and mantle timing changing, or the same inputs twice giving different state.

swimming.catches: Swimming in open deep water changing: floating at the surface, stroke speed, drawing and stowing the gun, and diving.

face.catches: Idle blinks (12 to 40 a minute, never in sync across 50 kongs), expressions reaching their targets within 0.3 s, or gaze going past its limits.

anim.catches: Planted feet sliding, third-person reload animation drifting from the sim's reload flag, or hands leaving the weapon.

walkgraph.catches: The building walk graph: window glass must block walking but not sight, stair heights must resolve, and a staircase must stay connected.

solver.catches: Capsule solver acceptance tests: the real step code against test boxes and against stuck spots found in live matches, each also run on the old solver for comparison.

glass.catches: Breakable glass: every way to break a pane (shot, punch, sprint, rocket), window vaults, and the break events on the wire, including for a late joiner.

planeview.catches: In low-memory mode, the plane queuing locations that are out of view or fewer than are in view (up to 2), or the chase camera seeing locations on too few paths.
planeview.label: Low-memory plane queues the locations in view

raycast.catches: StaticWorld.raycast disagreeing with a reference walk: exact ties between boxes and thousands of seeded random rays must give the same hit.

res.catches: Resource scopes not disposing their geometry, material and texture when closed, in order, or the ledger miscounting bytes by category.

refresh.catches: The display refresh estimate: a slow game must still read as the screen's real rate (60, 120, 144 Hz), and real 30 Hz pacing must read 30.

resguard.catches: The half-rate guard lowering 3D resolution when it shouldn't, going below Auto's floor, not stepping back up after full-rate seconds, or oscillating.

parity.catches: Five checks, each asserted against its own expected result: network snapshots, the matrix cache, the geometry index, static file serving and splat viewport selection.

sim.catches: A headless 50-bot match with no winner, friendly-fire hits, bots not arming up, tick cost over budget, a vehicle seat and its rider disagreeing, an illegal phase change, or a final state hash that differs from the recorded one.

nettail.catches: A network tail (slowest 1% of input replies) that gets worse.

afk.label: AFK removal returns the player to the waiting area (real server)
afk.catches: An idle player not being taken out of the match, kept in the waiting area with the reason shown, while active players carry on, tested against the real server.

redteam.label: Red team checks on the admin tools
redteam.catches: Hostile use of a server tool; the details stay out of this page.

wt.catches: The WebTransport endpoint: off by default, refused on a wrong token or a second session, inputs and snapshots as datagrams with lost windows repaired, a session that floods the server being closed, and the A/B arm counted in /health.

wtbrowser.catches: WebTransport in headless Chromium against a real server: arm selection, ping and pong, the session outliving a quiet period, fallback to WebSockets when the server closes it, and the flag overrides. It passes with SKIP when no browser or QUIC build is present.

test.label: build and test
test.catches: Runs npm run build and the whole npm test list above.

secrets.label: no secrets
secrets.catches: Keys, tokens or environment files committed to the repo (gitleaks).

boot.label: no-GPU boot smoke
boot.catches: A production build that doesn't boot in software-rendered Chromium (smoke only, not frame rate or looks), or holds more memory at the title than its budget.

memory.label: no-GPU match-to-match memory
memory.catches: Memory that grows from one match to the next, or resources no scope owns.

lowmem-memory.label: no-GPU low-memory memory
lowmem-memory.catches: More memory than budget in the low-memory setup: at the title, in the plane and 60 s into play.

context-restore.label: no-GPU context restore
context-restore.catches: A WebGL context lost at the title or in a match warm-up that doesn't restore.

coming.name: Allocation per host tick
coming.plain: Bytes allocated per server tick become a budget in npm test.

coming.name: PR metrics comment
coming.plain: Every budgeted number, main against the PR, as a comment on each PR.

coming.name: Tick A/B
coming.plain: Main-thread time per tick compared between main and the PR on the same machine.

coming.name: Visual diffs
coming.plain: Same-camera stills compared between main and the PR.

coming.name: A location is never invisible
coming.plain: A runtime check that no location in view is missing from the frame.

coming.name: Protocol fuzzing
coming.plain: Malformed frames thrown at the wire decoder to check it never crashes a match.
